Hi John —

Thanks again for the call today — great context on FintechX's roadmap and where LLM features fit into your product. Below is a quick recap and the specific items we said we'd follow up on: 

Recap (short):
- Primary use: document summarization + customer intent classification in the onboarding flow.
- Expected active users hitting LLM features: 100k MAU initially, ramp to ~500k over 12 months.
- Typical request sizes: 250–800 tokens per interaction (summaries ~600 tokens).
- Target latency: P95 < 300ms for interactive parts; background batches ok to be higher.

Follow-ups / asks from our side:
1) Please confirm a monthly token volume range (conservative / expected / optimistic).
2) Any spend/budget guardrails or target $/1M tokens you have in mind?
3) Who on procurement should we loop in for pricing approvals (if different from Samir)?

Next steps I propose:
- You send the volume ranges (item 1) and Samir confirms budget range.
- Rafael will outline caching/batching opportunities and a first-pass $/feature and $/1M-token estimate.
- I'll share the Redwood pricing sheet and a sample unit-econ model we can adapt.

I've attached our current pricing sheet and an estimate template — Rafael and I will prepare a short unit-econ playbook for the deep dive. Can we aim for a 30–45 minute follow-up on Wednesday 10/20?

Best,

Thanks for the follow-up and for the clear recap. Quick answers below (Samir included for budget confirmation):

Monthly token volume (three scenarios):
- Conservative: 200M tokens/month (pilot period, 3 months)
- Expected: 850M tokens/month (6–9 months post-launch)
- Optimistic: 2.1B tokens/month (12–18 months if feature adoption is high)

Budget guardrails:
- Initial procurement target: <$40K/month during pilot (we can stretch to $60K/month if ROI is clear).
- Longer-term finance target: $150–200K/month fixed budget for inference if unit economics justify it.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: John Davies <john.davies@fintechx.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Unit economics deep dive — next steps

John / team —

Appreciate the volume ranges — helpful. A few quick notes on levers we typically use to get to that $30–$50/1M target and how that maps to feature-level economics: 

1) Model tiering + routing: route non-critical background summarization to cheaper quantized models (e.g., q4_8b) and keep high-quality LLMs for interactive flows. Savings: ~30–60% on per-token cost depending on quality needs.

2) Prefix/KV caching for repeat content (onboarding flows often have high overlap): can reduce compute by 20–40% on read-heavy flows.

3) Aggressive batching for background jobs (end-of-day summarization): effective $/1M improvement vs interactive by ~2–3x for the same model.

4) Payload engineering: shorter prompts + structured outputs to cut prompt and completion tokens by 15–25%.

Preliminary ballpark unit-econ examples (using your expected 850M tokens/mo):
- Raw inference cost (no caching/batching optimizations): ~$55–75 per 1M tokens -> monthly inference cost $46k–$64k.
- With model tiering + caching + prompt optimizations (reasonable): ~$30–40 per 1M tokens -> monthly inference cost $25.5k–$34k.

$/feature example (customer onboarding summary):
- Avg tokens per feature call: 650 tokens (prompt+completion).
- At $35 / 1M tokens -> cost per call = 0.00065 * 35 = ~$0.0228 (~2.3 cents)
- If we cache common prefixes and reduce average tokens to 450 -> cost per call = 0.01575 (~1.6 cents)

CAC payback scenarios (very high level):
- If feature monetizes to $0.20 ARPU per call and average user uses feature 3x/month, gross revenue/user/month = $0.60.
- With inference cost per user/month (assuming 3 calls at $0.0228) = $0.0684.
- Contribution margin before CAC & infra = ~88%. With ~ $50 CAC, payback around 83 months — obviously we need higher monetization or lower CAC / higher frequency.

Margin targets vs inference cost: enterprise teams we work with target 60–70% gross margin after inference cost (i.e., inference < 30–40% of gross margin line items). That usually implies a target inference cost per user/month < $0.10 for B2B monetized features.

I'll prepare a one-page unit-econ model for Wednesday that lets you plug in your ARPU, CAC, and adoption assumptions.

Rafael
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
